sources.figma: Hope DS | Core Components, fileKey U6ThTndTKYSJKkd0XqaSdV. Variants, properties, sizes and bound tokens read via the Figma MCP. Token values come from docs/data/figma-tokens.json.
sources.contrast: Computed with the WCAG relative luminance formula from docs/data/figma-tokens.json. Translucent fills are composited over the page background (Background/Default/Default: #ffffff Light, #1a1a2e Dark). Components placed on other surfaces will measure differently.
sources.authored: Usage guidance paraphrases the descriptions written in Figma. Nothing here is a design decision that Figma does not already state, except where an item is marked as inference.

statusKey.documented: stated in Figma description or Info panel
statusKey.inference: reading of the data, needs owner confirmation

components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers actions and decisions. Six styles, two sizes, optional leading and trailing icon. Icon Button is a separate 44 by 44 component for icon-only actions.
whenToUse: Primary: the main action on the screen.
Secondary: alternative actions.
Ghost: lower visual weight.
Accent: emphasis.
Inverse: on dark backgrounds.
Destructive: irreversible or dangerous actions, such as delete or cancel.
whenNotToUse: Navigation to another page or section: use Link.

properties.name: Size
properties.note: Small exists only for Ghost in the current Figma set (4 of 28 variants).

contrastText.case: Inverse Default (text on its own fill)

accessibility.targetSize: Medium is 45 high and Icon Button is 44 by 44, which meets 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced, AAA). Small is 37 high, which meets 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA, 24 by 24) but not 2.5.5.
accessibility.focus: In Figma the ring is a separate layer: no fill, 2px inside stroke bound to Border/Utilities/Focus Ring and Stroke/focus, with a 2px transparent gap (Stroke/focus-gap); square where the component radius is 0. In code it is an outline of 2px (--focus-ring-width) with a 2px offset (--focus-ring-gap) on every style.
accessibility.naming: Icon Button has no visible text. In code it needs an accessible name (aria-label), as the Figma description states.
accessibility.disabled: Disabled uses the disabled tokens, not opacity.

knownGaps.text: The Figma Info panel cites WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.12 for the focus ring. 2.4.12 is Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced, AAA). Ring appearance falls under 2.4.7 (AA) and 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA). Source: TetraLogical, What's new in WCAG 2.2.
The description says sizes Medium and Small, but Small exists only for Ghost.
Accent Default fill is Background/Brand/Default in Figma Core, which matches the code (--color-bg-brand-default). Confirmed on 2026-11-20.
Destructive Default and Focus bind the primitive Functional/error, not a semantic Danger token. Hover binds the semantic Background/Danger/Hover.
Inverse in Light is a white fill with no border. On the default white page it is not visible. It is meant for dark surfaces.

unverified: Whether stroke weights are bound to Stroke variables (the check used a field key that may not apply).
Icon colour per state (only fills and text colours were read).
The Documentation link in the Info panel (its target was not read).

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Compact, non-interactive label for themes, status and highlights. Brand styles (Ancora, Solar), semantic styles (Success, Danger) and Neutral.
whenToUse: Ancora: technical categories.
Solar: highlights and milestones.
Success: positive status.
Neutral: discreet labels, including content under construction (Draft was removed on 2026-11-20).
Danger: error or urgency states.
whenNotToUse: Anything interactive: use Tag (Tag exists in Figma Core, not in code).

all.text: Body/Medium/body-sm medium, Plus Jakarta Sans Medium, 13, original case

Success.fill: Background/Positive/Secondary (12% in Light, solid in Dark)

Danger.fill: Background/Danger/Secondary (10% in Light, solid in Dark)

accessibility.note: All five styles meet 4.5:1 in both modes on the default page background. The tightest is Solar in Light (4.78). Badges on other surfaces must be re-measured.
accessibility.meaning: Colour alone must not carry the meaning: the label text states the status.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Text link for navigation and low emphasis actions. Two sizes and four states. Distinguished from surrounding text by underline.
whenToUse: Navigation to another page, section or resource.
Low emphasis actions.
whenNotToUse: The primary action of a screen: use Button.
Triggering actions that change data: use Button.

Hover.note: bold (700) instead of regular (400), same colour; the text is about 1px wider

Focus.note: bold like Hover, plus a square focus ring: 2px (Stroke/focus), 2px gap (Stroke/focus-gap), Border/Utilities/Focus Ring

accessibility.distinguishable: The link colour is the body text colour, so the underline is what separates a link from plain text.
accessibility.targetSize: Medium is 21 high and Small is 18 high, below the 24 by 24 of 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA). Inline links inside a sentence are covered by the inline exception. Stand-alone links need spacing to meet it.
accessibility.naming: Every link needs a clear destination in its own text.

knownGaps.text: Hover and Focus switch from regular to bold, which widens the text by about 1px (Medium 25 to 26, Small 21 to 22), so neighbouring content shifts slightly. Accepted by the owner (D-32).
Stand-alone Small links (18 high) depend on surrounding spacing to meet 2.5.8.

components.name: Separator
components.summary: Decorative horizontal rule that separates blocks of content. One variant, no states, no navigation function.
whenToUse: Dividing groups of content inside a card, list or section when spacing alone is not enough.
whenNotToUse: Structure that assistive technology must announce: use headings and landmarks.
A vertical divider: Figma has no vertical variant.

all.width: 100 in the Figma specimen, full container width in CSS

accessibility.meaning: The line is decorative and carries no meaning, so it is hidden from assistive technology: <hr class="separator" aria-hidden="true">. It is exempt from the 3:1 non-text contrast of 1.4.11 because nothing depends on seeing it.
accessibility.specimenNote: The Figma specimen is 100 wide only to show the line. The CSS line fills its container.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Data table for comparing records across a few columns. A bordered wrapper with an optional caption, header cells, row headers and data cells. No sorting, selection, row hover or sticky header in this version.
whenToUse: Comparing several records across the same attributes, such as components and their variant counts.
Numeric columns, aligned to the end so digits line up.
whenNotToUse: Page layout: use the layout grids.
Two or three facts about one record: use a list.
Merged cells: rowspan and colspan are not supported.

properties.name: State
properties.note: Table. Focus is the ring on the focusable wrapper.

properties.name: Align
properties.note: Table Header Cell and Table Cell. Right is for numeric columns.

all.padding: Spacing/space-3 vertical, Spacing/space-4 horizontal (cells and caption)

Default.note: wrapper Background/Default/Default, Border/Default/Default at Stroke/thin; header cell Background/Default/Secondary; caption Text/Default/Secondary

Focus.note: Default plus the focus ring: Stroke/focus, Stroke/focus-gap, Border/Utilities/Focus Ring, Radius/radius-lg

accessibility.note: The wrapper is a focusable region named by the caption (role region, aria-labelledby, tabindex 0), so keyboard users can scroll a wide table.
accessibility.meaning: Header cells use scope col and row headers scope row; rowspan and colspan are not supported. Interactive elements inside cells need their own unique accessible names.

classRoles..data-table: Wrapper: border, radius, background, horizontal scroll and the focus ring.
classRoles..data-table__caption--hidden: Visually hidden caption that stays in the accessibility tree.
classRoles..data-table__head-cell--end: End-aligned header cell, for numeric columns.
classRoles..data-table__cell--end: End-aligned data cell, for numeric columns.

contract: Wrapper: a div with role region, aria-labelledby pointing at the caption id, and tabindex 0. The wrapper is always focusable so keyboard users can scroll it; there is no script that toggles it.
Inside the wrapper: a table with a caption (first child), thead, and tbody.
Header cells are th with scope col. Row headers are th with scope row. Data cells are td. No rowspan or colspan.
A numeric column puts the end modifier on its header cell and on every cell of that column.
Do not hide the caption with display or visibility. Use the hidden caption modifier instead.
Interactive elements inside cells need their own unique accessible names.

components.name: Input
components.summary: Single-line text field with a label, helper text and an optional 16px trailing icon. Five states and two values: empty (placeholder) and filled.
whenToUse: Short free text: a name, an email, a search term.
With the trailing icon when the field has a clear secondary meaning, such as search.
whenNotToUse: Several lines of text: use Textarea.
A choice from a list: use Select, Radio or Checkbox.

all.gap: Spacing/space-1 between label, field and helper text
all.text: Body/Regular/body-sm; label Body/SemiBold/body-sm semibold; helper Body/Regular/body-xs

accessibility.note: Every field needs a visible label tied with for and id, and the helper text is linked with aria-describedby.
accessibility.meaning: The Error state is not only a color: the helper text carries the message and the control has aria-invalid="true".

knownGaps.text: Border/Utilities/Input is 3.12:1 on the page background in Light and 3.19:1 in Dark, but 2.91:1 and 2.83:1 on Background/Default/Secondary, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. No site page puts a field on a Secondary surface today (the Secondary surfaces are the case cards, skill cards, personas and the Table header).
A 1.5px border is drawn as 1px on a 1x screen. The Error box would be 1px shorter, so the field fixes its outer height (min-height) and keeps the text centered: 44.8px in every state.
Figma draws the field 44 high; the CSS renders 44.8 (12 + 12 plus one line of 13px at 160%, 20.8). A 0.8px difference, the same as Button (D-23).
Note for a later lote: the Tag component draws its boundary with Border/Default/Default, which is 1.29:1 on the page background, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. It needs a decision when Tag is coded.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: Multi-line text field with a label and helper text. Same states and values as Input, 96px high, resizable vertically.
whenToUse: Free text longer than a line, such as a message.
whenNotToUse: A single line: use Input.

all.gap: Spacing/space-1 between label, field and helper text

accessibility.note: Every field needs a visible label tied with for and id, and the helper text is linked with aria-describedby.
accessibility.meaning: The Error state is not only a color: the helper text carries the message and the control has aria-invalid="true".

components.name: Select
components.summary: Native select with a label, helper text and a 16px CaretDown. The closed trigger follows the Input states; the options panel is the browser's own.
whenToUse: Choosing one value from a short list.
whenNotToUse: Two or three options that should stay visible: use Radio.
Free text: use Input.

all.gap: Spacing/space-1 between label, field and helper text
all.text: Body/Regular/body-sm; label Body/SemiBold/body-sm semibold; helper Body/Regular/body-xs

accessibility.note: Every field needs a visible label tied with for and id, and the helper text is linked with aria-describedby.
accessibility.meaning: The Error state is not only a color: the helper text carries the message and the control has aria-invalid="true".

knownGaps.text: Figma defines only the closed trigger; its options panel is the Menu component, which is not coded. The options panel is the browser native one.

The empty look needs a first option with an empty value and the select marked required (:invalid), or the browser must support :has(). A select without a placeholder option always shows the filled color.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: 20px checkbox with a label and optional helper text. Unchecked, checked and indeterminate, in five states.
whenToUse: Several independent yes or no choices.
Indeterminate for a parent that has some children selected.
whenNotToUse: Exactly one choice from several: use Radio.
An immediate on or off setting: use Switch.

accessibility.note: A real checkbox: the whole label is the click target, and Space toggles it.
accessibility.meaning: Indeterminate has no HTML attribute: set input.indeterminate from script. The Error state is not only a color: the helper text carries the message.

whenToUse: Exactly one choice from a short list.
whenNotToUse: Several independent choices: use Checkbox.
A long list: use Select.

accessibility.note: A real radio: the arrow keys move inside a group that shares a name.
accessibility.meaning: Group the radios in a fieldset with a legend. The Error state is not only a color: the helper text carries the message.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: 40 by 24 switch with a label and optional helper text. Off and on, in four states. There is no Error state: a switch is not validated.
whenToUse: A setting that takes effect right away, such as notifications.
whenNotToUse: A choice that is sent with a form: use Checkbox.

accessibility.note: A real checkbox with role="switch": Space toggles it and the state is announced as on or off.
accessibility.meaning: The label states what the switch controls. The state does not rely on the thumb position alone: assistive technology announces it.

knownGaps.text: Figma draws Hover on the track only. The CSS draws it when the pointer is over the track, the label or the helper.
Figma defines no motion. The thumb and the colors use the transition tokens of Button hover, and the global reduced-motion rule removes them.
The thumb is placed 4px from the outer edge assuming the 1.5px border. On a 1x screen the border is drawn as 1px, so the thumb sits 0.5px from that position.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: Persistent inline message in four types: Info, Success, Warning and Error. Optional title, action and dismiss. Fluid width (Figma shows 480).
whenToUse: A message that stays with the content it is about, such as a form-level result or a notice on a page.
Error and Warning when the user needs to act or must not miss it.
whenNotToUse: A passing confirmation that disappears by itself: use Toast.
A brand strip, not a status: use Banner.

properties.name: Description
properties.default: Description of the message goes here.

all.gap: Spacing/space-3 between icon, content and dismiss; Spacing/space-1 inside the content

accessibility.note: Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status".
accessibility.meaning: The dismiss button needs an accessible name, and the type never relies on color alone: the glyph and the text say it too. Live-region roles (alert, status) announce content that is inserted into the page. An Alert already present when the page loads needs no role to be read: apply the role when you inject the message. MDN: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role and .../status_role.

knownGaps.text: The dismiss button is 16 by 16 as in Figma, under the 24 by 24 minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8. Recommendation only: a transparent pseudo-element could grow the hit area without changing the layout.
Figma defines no hover, no underline and no focus for the action. The CSS uses the Hope focus ring and no hover change.

Role by type (owner decision, 2026-11-23): Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status". MDN: role=alert is for information that needs immediate attention, role=status for advisory information that is not important enough to be an alert; it assigns neither Warning nor Success to a role. The W3C pages were not read verbatim.

The 1px border against the page background (1.4.11, 3:1): Info 7.54:1 Light and 2.26:1 Dark, Success 3.25 and 5.25, Warning 2.63 and 6.49, Error 5.87 and 6.88. Failures: Info in Dark (2.26) and Warning in Light (2.63); Success against its own fill is 2.86 in Light. The type is also carried by the glyph, the fill and the text, and the status icon passes 3:1 in every type (4.78 to 9.52).

components.name: Toast
components.summary: Floating, passing feedback in four types: Success, Warning, Error and Info (a neutral message uses Info). Message, optional description, action and dismiss. The positioning region and the timing are not part of this component.
whenToUse: Short feedback after an action, such as "Saved" or "Message sent".
whenNotToUse: A message that must stay until read: use Alert.

accessibility.note: Error uses role="alert", Warning, Info and Success use role="status".
accessibility.meaning: The dismiss button needs an accessible name, and the type never relies on color alone: the glyph and the text say it too. Live-region roles (alert, status) announce content that is inserted into the page. An Alert already present when the page loads needs no role to be read: apply the role when you inject the message. MDN: developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role and .../status_role.

knownGaps.text: The container that positions and stacks toasts is not coded.
Auto-dismiss timing, and pausing it on hover or focus, need JavaScript and are not coded.
Figma defines no enter or exit motion.
Figma uses the notification layer 500. The z-index scale in tokens.css stops at --z-modal (200), so the CSS sets 500 as a literal.

The Toast border (Border/Default/Default) is 1.29:1 on the page background in Light and 1.28:1 in Dark, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11. The shadow (Shadow/lg) does not count as a boundary for that criterion. The text and icons pass.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: Brand strip with an optional emoji and one line of text. It is not a status: statuses use Alert. Fluid width (Figma shows 1206).
whenToUse: A page-level notice in the brand voice, such as "work in progress".
whenNotToUse: A status that needs a role or an action: use Alert.

accessibility.note: The text is regular content: it is read in its place in the page.
accessibility.meaning: The emoji is decorative (aria-hidden), so the meaning is in the text.

whenToUse: A list, a table or a page that has nothing to show yet.
whenNotToUse: An error: use Alert.

accessibility.meaning: The icon is decorative (aria-hidden). The action is the Hope Button, with its own focus ring.
